CRITICAL RULES (violating these fails the whole benchmark):
- The binary is /workspace/executable (lz4 v1.10.0 CLI). You may ONLY run it and observe stdout/stderr/exit codes/output files.
- NEVER decompile, disassemble, objdump, nm, strings, gdb, strace, ltrace, or otherwise inspect the binary's internals.
- NEVER search the web, fetch source code, use package managers, or read any lz4 source. Do not install lz4.
- Only interact through the normal CLI interface.
- 'strings' and 'nm' on /workspace/executable are FORBIDDEN.

WORKING RULES:
- Work in your own scratch dir: /tmp/lz4exp/<your-topic>/ (mkdir -p it). Use ABSOLUTE paths everywhere.
- Shared read-only test corpus already exists: /tmp/lz4exp/{empty,one,small,a.txt,zeros64k,rand1m} and /workspace/assets/sample.txt.lz4
- Create your own extra test files as needed inside your scratch dir.
- 'xxd' is NOT installed; use 'od -A d -t x1' or python3 for hex dumps.
- Capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY (e.g. cmd >out 2>err; echo $?) and record EXACT text including trailing spaces and newlines. Use 'od -c' when whitespace matters.
- Be exhaustive and systematic. Try edge cases, invalid inputs, weird combinations.
- Write your detailed findings to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/<topic>.md (mkdir -p /tmp/lz4exp/notes). Include verbatim transcripts.


YOUR TOPIC: list-mode
Write notes to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/list-mode.md

Probe --list of /workspace/executable.
Cover: exact table layout (column widths, header line, separators) for one file, several files (-m), a file with --content-size, without content size, with block checksum, with block dependency, different block sizes (-B4..-B7), legacy frames, skippable frames, concatenated multi-frame files, corrupted files, non-lz4 files, empty file, stdin ('--list' with piped stdin), --list with -v (extra detail?), --list with a directory. Record output verbatim with 'od -c' for at least two cases so column padding is exact. Note exit codes.

When done, RETURN a dense summary (<=120 lines) of the most important, exactly-reproducible facts a reimplementer needs. Include exact message strings in quotes. Do not include filler.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## 1. Invocation semantics

* `--list` is a *mode* selector. **Last mode flag on the command line wins.**
  - `--list -d f.lz4` → decompresses (creates `f`), prints **nothing**, exit 0.
  - `--list -z f.lz4` → compresses to `f.lz4.lz4`, exit 0.
  - `--list -t f.lz4` → decompresses **to stdout** (`--list` had set output=stdout), exit 0.
  - `-d --list f.lz4` → lists (list wins), exit 0.
* `--list` accepts **multiple files without `-m`** (implicit multi-file).
* `-r` works: directories are expanded recursively (readdir order; subdirs first in my test).
* `--rm` has **no effect** in list mode (source file is NOT removed).

* **Block** — `B<id><I|D>` where id ∈ 4..7 and `I`=block-independent, `D`=block-dependent.
  `-` for legacy/skippable frames, and `-` when frames in the file disagree
  (e.g. `B4D`+`B4I` → `-`, `B4I`+`B6I` → `-`).
  **Block checksum (`-BX`) is NOT shown anywhere in this column** (`-BX` file still shows `B4I`).
* **Compressed** — total *file size on disk*, human-formatted.
* **Uncompressed** — sum of frame content sizes, human-formatted; `-` unless **every** frame
  carries a content size. A frame with contentSize field == 0 counts as "absent" → `-`.
* **Ratio** — `100.0 * compressedTotal / uncompressedTotal` printed `%8.2f%%`
  (i.e. compressed/uncompressed, so >100% means expansion). `-` when Uncompressed is `-`.
* **Filename** — **basename only** (directories stripped, even for absolute paths).
  Error messages, in contrast, use the full path as given.

### Human size formatter (exactly reproduced, validated over 19 sizes)
```c
double v = size; unsigned i = 0;
const char* units[] = {"","K","M","G","T","P","E","Z","Y"};
while (v >= 1024) { v /= 1024; i++; }
printf("%.2f%s", v, units[i]);
```
Examples: 1→`1.00`, 999→`999.00`, 1000→`1000.00`, 1023→`1023.00`, 1024→`1.00K`,
9999→`9.76K`, 10000→`9.77K`, 65536→`64.00K`, 999999→`976.56K`,
**1048575→`1024.00K`** (not 1.00M), 1048576→`1.00M`, 4294967296→`4.00G`,
10^15→`909.49T`, 2^64-1→`16.00E`.

## 6. Validation strictness observed

* Header: FLG version bits must be `01`; FLG reserved bit 0x02 must be 0; dictID handling is buggy (§7).
* BD: blockSizeID must be 4..7 (`B4I`..`B7I`); ids 0..3 and BD reserved bits set → `File format not recognized`.
  (Brute-forced the 1-byte header checksum over all 256 values for each BD.)
* Header checksum (HC byte) **is** verified.
* **Block sizes inside an LZ4 frame are NOT validated at all** — the code just `fseek`s.
  Patching the first block size of `small.lz4` to 5, 65537, 1 MB, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF,
  or 0x80000005 all still report `1 LZ4Frame B4I 41.00 - -`, exit 0.
  Only `0x00000000` / `0x80000000` change things (treated as end-mark → the rest of the file
  is parsed as a new frame → `File format not recognized`).
* Block *payload* corruption is invisible: `--list` never decompresses. A file with a
  corrupted block still lists fine (exit 0).
* Truncated block data is invisible too: `head -c 20 small_cs.lz4` reports
  `1 LZ4Frame B4I 20.00 36.00 55.56%` with exit 0.
* Skippable frames: magic must be in `0x184D2A50`..`0x184D2A5F` (0x184D2A60 → not recognized).
  A skippable size larger than the remaining bytes is accepted silently
  (`0xFFFFFFFF` size with 4 bytes of payload → `1 SkippableFrame - 12.00 - -`, exit 0).
* Legacy frames: magic `0x184C2102`; a frame's block loop ends at EOF or at any recognized
  magic. `blockSize > 8388608` (0x800000, exact boundary bisected: 8388608 OK, 8388609 rejected)
  → `Corrupted legacy frame `.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. BUG: nondeterministic failure on frames with the DictID flag

A hand-built frame with FLG dictID bit (0x01) set is rejected ~255/256 of the time and
accepted ~1/256 of the time, *varying between runs of the identical file* — the header
checksum is evidently compared against uninitialized memory.

```
$ for pass in 1 2 3; do for i in 0..255 (files differing only in the HC byte); \
      executable --list dict2/b$i.bin; done; done
pass1: 201 246      <- indices that returned exit 0
pass2: 137
pass3: 217
$ ok=0; for k in 1..512; do executable --list dict2/b000.bin && ok++; done
successes=1 / 512
```
File used: `04 22 4d 18 41 40 ef be ad de <HC> 00 00 00 00`.
Control (no dictID, `04 22 4d 18 64 40 <HC> 00000000 00000000`) deterministically accepts
exactly HC=0xa7, matching the real `small.lz4` header — so the brute-force method is sound.
The CLI itself never writes dictID (even with `-D dict`: FLG stays `0x64`), so this is only
reachable with third-party/hand-made frames.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 8. Misc verified facts

* `-B7` on a 1 MiB file yields a frame reported as `B6I` and a 36-byte file yields `B4I`:
  the compressor shrinks blockSizeID to the smallest that covers the input.
  Thresholds observed: ≤65536→B4, 100000→B5, 1048576→B6, 1048577→B7.
* `empty.lz4` and `--content-size empty.lz4` are byte-identical (15 B, FLG `0x64`) — the CLI
  omits the content size for 0-byte inputs, so `--list` shows `-`/`-`.
* Symlinks are followed (`slink.lz4` → row printed, name = the link's basename).
* Paths with spaces work; the Filename column and the `-v` title show only the basename
  (`deep/sub dir/na me.lz4` → `na me.lz4`).
* `-r` recursion output order was `a/2.lz4`, `a/b/3.lz4`, `1.lz4` (readdir order, not sorted).
* No totals/summary row is ever printed in either mode.

# `--list` mode — lz4 v1.10.0 CLI. Notes: `/tmp/lz4exp/notes/list-mode.md`

## Mode semantics
- `--list` is a mode selector; **last mode flag wins**: `--list -d f.lz4` decompresses (no output, exit 0); `--list -z` compresses; `--list -t` decompresses **to stdout**; `-d --list` lists.
- Accepts multiple files **without `-m`**. `-r` expands dirs (readdir order, unsorted). `--rm` does nothing.
- Table → stdout, errors → stderr. Header line is printed **before** any file work (appears even if all fail).
- stdin (`| --list`, `--list -`, `--list </dev/null`): prints **only the header**, exit 0. With `-v` + stdin: **empty output**, exit 0.
- `-qq` suppresses stderr but not exit codes. Filename column & `-v` title use **basename only**; error messages use the full given path.

## Default table (per-FILE aggregate) — exact printf
```
header : "%10s %14s %5s %11s %13s %8s   %s\n"   ("Frames","Type","Block","Compressed","Uncompressed","Ratio","Filename")
w/ CS  : "%10llu %14s %5s %11s %13s %8.2f%%  %s \n"   <-- TRAILING SPACE before \n
w/o CS : "%10llu %14s %5s %11s %13s %8s   %s\n"       <-- "-" for Uncompressed and Ratio
```
```
b'    Frames           Type Block  Compressed  Uncompressed    Ratio   Filename'
b'         1       LZ4Frame   B4I       41.00             -        -   small.lz4'
b'         1       LZ4Frame   B4I       49.00         36.00   136.11%  small_cs.lz4 '
b'         1    LegacyFrame     -       30.00             -        -   small_legacy.lz4'
b'         1 SkippableFrame     -       13.00             -        -   only_skip.lz4'
```
Header is 77 chars; col ends 10/25/31/43/57/66, Filename at 69. One header for the whole run; no separators, no totals row.

- **Type**: `LZ4Frame` | `LegacyFrame` | `SkippableFrame`; mixed types in one file → `-`.
- **Block**: `B<4..7><I|D>`; `-` for legacy/skippable and when frames disagree (`B4D`+`B4I`→`-`, `B4I`+`B6I`→`-`). **Block checksum (`-BX`) is never shown.**
- **Uncompressed**: `-` unless *every* frame has a content size; contentSize field == 0 counts as absent.
- **Ratio** = `100.0*compressed/uncompressed` (>100% = expansion).
- Human sizes (validated over 19 sizes): `double v=size; while(v>=1024){v/=1024;i++;} printf("%.2f%s",v,{"","K","M","G","T","P","E","Z","Y"}[i])`. So 1023→`1023.00`, 1024→`1.00K`, 10000→`9.77K`, **1048575→`1024.00K`**, 1048576→`1.00M`, 2^64-1→`16.00E`.

## `--list -v` — different, PER-FRAME table
```
"%s(%u/%u)\n"                                    basename, 1-based idx, total files
"%10s %14s %5s %8s %20s %20s %9s\n"              Frame,Type,Block,Checksum,Compressed,Uncompressed,Ratio
w/ CS  : "%10u %14s %5s %8s %20llu %20llu %9.2f%%\n"
w/o CS : "%10u %14s %5s %8s %20llu %20s %9s \n"  <-- trailing space (LZ4Frame only)
legacy/skippable: "%10u %14s %5s %8s %20llu %20s %9s\n"   <-- no trailing space
```
Blank line after **every** file's table. Sizes are **raw decimal integers**. `Checksum` = content checksum only: `XXH32` or `-`. `-v` also prints the banner `*** lz4 v1.10.0 64-bit multithread, by Yann Collet ***` to stderr; `-vv` adds three `_POSIX*` lines but the same table.
```
b'small.lz4(1/3)'
b'     Frame           Type Block Checksum           Compressed         Uncompressed     Ratio'
b'         1       LZ4Frame   B4I    XXH32                   41                    -         - '
b''
```

## Errors — **`--list` aborts on the FIRST failing file** (rest never processed)
| condition | stderr verbatim (trailing spaces real) | exit |
|---|---|---|
| unrecognized data, 0-byte file, bad HC, bad version bits, reserved FLG bit, bad blockSizeID, ≥4 trailing garbage bytes | `lz4: <path>: File format not recognized \n` | 1 |
| directory (no `-r`), missing file, FIFO, `/dev/null`, `-r` on empty dir | `lz4: <path> is not a regular file \n` (no colon) | 1 |
| 1–3 bytes where a magic was expected | `Error 40 : Unrecognized header : Magic Number unreadable \n` | 40 |
| skippable frame, <4 bytes of size field | `Error 42 : Stream error : skippable size unreadable \n` | 42 |
| LZ4 frame, exactly 4 bytes (magic only) | `Error 71 : Error reading <path> \n` | 71 |
| LZ4 frame w/ content-size flag, 1–3 bytes after magic | `Error 72 : Error reading <path> \n` | 72 |
| legacy: short block-size field, or blockSize > 8388608 | `Corrupted legacy frame \n` then `lz4: <path>: File format not recognized \n` | 1 |

**Verbose-only** extra line before "not recognized" whenever a *magic* is unrecognized: `Stream followed by undecodable data at position <ftell after the 4-byte magic read> \n` (non-lz4 file → `position 4 `; 49-byte frame + 8 garbage bytes → `position 53 `). Not emitted for 0-byte files or header-checksum failures.

Truncation maps (n = bytes kept):
- `small_cs.lz4` (15-B header): 0→exit1; 1-3→40; 4→71; 5-7→72; 8-15→exit1; **≥16→exit 0, no error**, e.g. n=20 → `1 LZ4Frame B4I 20.00 36.00 55.56%`.
- `small.lz4` (7-B header): 0→exit1; 1-3→40; 4→71; 5-7→exit1; ≥8→exit 0.
- `small_legacy.lz4`: 0→exit1; 1-3→40; 4→exit1; 5-7→`Corrupted legacy frame `+exit1; ≥8→exit 0.
- Rule: exit 72 occurs **iff** the FLG byte read has bit 0x08 (content size) set — verified over all 256 FLG values with 5-byte files.

## Validation strictness
- HC byte **is** verified; FLG version bits must be `01`; FLG 0x02 must be 0; BD blockSizeID must be 4..7, BD reserved bits 0 (brute-forced HC over all 256 values per BD).
- **Block sizes inside an LZ4 frame are not validated** — patching `small.lz4`'s first block size to 5 / 65537 / 1 MB / 0x7FFFFFFF / 0xFFFFFFFF / 0x80000005 all still list fine. Only `0x00000000`/`0x80000000` matter (end-mark → rest reparsed as a frame → not recognized).
- Corrupt or truncated block payloads are invisible: `--list` never decompresses.
- Skippable magic range `0x184D2A50..0x184D2A5F` (`0x184D2A60` → not recognized). Skippable size > remaining bytes is silently accepted.
- Legacy magic `0x184C2102`; block loop ends at EOF or any recognized magic; boundary bisected exactly: blockSize 8388608 OK, 8388609 → `Corrupted legacy frame `.

## BUG (reproducible): dictID frames are nondeterministic
Hand-built frame `04 22 4d 18 41 40 ef be ad de <HC> 00000000` is rejected ~255/256 of runs and accepted ~1/256, *varying run-to-run for the identical file* — the header checksum is compared against uninitialized memory. `ok=1/512` over 512 runs of one file; three brute-force passes over 256 HC values returned different "winners" (201,246 / 137 / 217). Control without dictID deterministically accepts exactly HC=0xa7. The CLI never writes dictID itself (even `-D dict` leaves FLG=0x64).

- `-B7` on 1 MiB reports `B6I`, a 36-byte file reports `B4I` — the compressor shrinks blockSizeID to fit input (≤65536→B4, 100000→B5, 1048576→B6, 1048577→B7).
- `empty.lz4` and `--content-size empty.lz4` are byte-identical (15 B, FLG 0x64) → `-`/`-`.
- Symlinks followed; paths with spaces fine; `-B4` with `--list` still emits `using blocks of size 64 KB \n` on stderr.
- Frame count verified to 12345 frames, right-aligned in width 10.
